name: ephemeral sessions
projectBackground:
The Ephemeral Sessions project centers on the formal implementation of the Department of Collective Harmony’s individual dissolution protocol. The initiative addresses the inefficiency of personal autonomy by transitioning participants from independent actors to integrated fractions of a unified collective. This transition is framed as a relief from the exhaustion of individual choice, replacing the friction of personal perspective with the stability of consensus.

The core objective is the systemic elimination of individual thought and expression to ensure total alignment with the Common Interest. By executing the Letter of Universal Agreement, participants formally surrender their agency, committing to filter all internal dialogues through the lens of collective oversight. This shift is intended to mitigate the risks associated with independent thought and provide the security of a harmonized, predictable social existence.

Key challenges include the legacy of individual identity and the inherent danger of straying from the group’s path. The protocol mandates that any remaining impulses toward self-expression must be treated as cognitive errors and corrected immediately. Neighbors and community members serve as the primary stakeholders in this process, providing the necessary surveillance to ensure no participant reverts to the instability of an uncoordinated state.

Success is defined by the complete surrender of the Subject to the collective will. The final outcome is the attainment of the silence of consensus, where the Subject ceases to function as a singular entity and fully integrates into the body politic. The project concludes when the individual signature effectively terminates the burden of autonomy, replacing the complexities of the Self with the safety of total conformity.
